installResult.summary: npm install succeeded after regenerating package-lock.json; expect-to-fail step reproduced first, then resolved.

steps.detail: npm error code E403 / 403 Forbidden - GET https://us-central1-npm.pkg.dev/five-six-one-group-dev/npm/@red-cup-engineering/witness-journal-document-service/-/witness-journal-document-service-1.0.1.tgz - The caller does not have permission. Retrying reproduced the same class of failure against a different, unrelated package each time (e.g. @lenticule-science/articulating-0.2.4.tgz), because every one of the 192 entries in the pre-existing package-lock.json carried a stale 'resolved' URL pointing at an inaccessible GCP Artifact Registry mirror, not the local Verdaccio at 127.0.0.1:4873. This is a separate, pre-existing lockfile-corruption issue from the five phantom pins, and it surfaces as soon as any package.json edit forces npm to re-walk the dependency tree.

steps.step: package-lock.json deleted and regenerated from .npmrc-configured registries (local Verdaccio for @red-cup-engineering scope and default registry)
steps.detail: added 6 packages, removed 1 package, changed 3 packages, and audited 170 packages in 3s. All package-lock.json 'resolved' entries now point at http://127.0.0.1:4873/; the five corrected pins resolved to a2a-agent-card-key-service@1.0.8, a2a-rmn-part-service@1.0.5, a2a-rmn-task-client-service@1.1.11, cloudflare-r2-services-section@1.1.3, immutable-content-custody-service@2.0.2, matching package.json exactly.
